title: Eye size and investment in frogs and toads correlate with adult habitat, activity pattern and breeding ecology (Dryad dataset: Thomas_species_traits.csv, 220 species with activity pattern and habitat)
note: Full text read (control-room oa job run 1): the article on PubMed Central (published version), not the Dryad data set named in the title and DOI. title: Feeding behavior and visual field differences in loggerhead and leatherback sea turtles may explain differences in longline fisheries interactions
note: Full text read (control-room oa job run 1), published version. The visual fields are given as areas at 20 cm (3550 cm2 leatherback; 11 278 cm2 for the loggerhead's two ellipses) and as a 60-degree loggerhead overlap; no horizontal or vertical field angle in degrees is stated in the text, so fov_h_deg for Dermochelys stays open.

title: Shining a Light on Patterns of Photoperiod Sensitivity in Germination and Flowering Across Latitudes, Ecosystems and Functional Traits
note: Full text read (control-room oa job run 1), published version (Europe PMC XML). Species values come from the Results text; the per-species metrics (Appendix S3, Table S3.1) and the flowering compilation (Appendix S2) are in the supplement, which was not in the text read. The Results say eleven of 67 species were significantly photoperiod-sensitive, the Discussion says 12. The reference list is empty in the text read.

title: Fuelling on the wing: sensory ecology of hawkmoth foraging
note: Full text read (control-room oa job run 1), published version (Europe PMC XML). A review, so every record is partial and names the cited study by author and year; the reference list is empty in the text read, and the text prints no volume or pages. Hemaris: the genus is named among the diurnal Macroglossinae genera, and Hemaris fuciformis has a wide-field motion-neuron optimum of 2 Hz; no Hemaris eye value (interommatidial angle, acuity, flicker) is given.

title: Psittacine Bird Ophthalmology: A Review of Anatomy, Physiology, Diagnostics, and Interventions
note: Full text read (control-room oa job run 1), published version (BioOne PDF). A review, so every record is partial and names the cited reference. Psittacula appears only in Table 1's clinical values (intraocular pressure, printed 'Psittacula krameria'); the review gives no visual-field, acuity or pigment value for Psittacula. The PDF text prints the degree sign as 8 (308 for 30 degrees), so degree values are written in words.

title: Floral scent in natural hybrids of Ipomopsis (Polemoniaceae) and their parental species
note: Full text read (control-room oa job run 1), published version (PubMed Central). Ipomopsis aggregata's day and night bouquets are compared in the text (alpha-pinene triples at night, aliphatics higher by day, indole virtually absent); the per-compound emission rates by day and night are in Supplementary Table S1, which was not in the text read. Natural hybrids were not logged as a taxon.
